items.q: Match the ARPKD ultrasound signs — 1) Echogenicity of the medulla  2) Corticomedullary differentiation … A) Lost  B) Hyperechoic
items.exp: USG in ARPKD: hyperechoic medulla with loss of corticomedullary differentiation. (Book p789)

items.q: The two ultrasound findings described in ARPKD are:
opts: Hyperechoic medulla and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
Hypoechoic medulla and preserved corticomedullary differentiation
Multiple cortical cysts with normal medulla
items.exp: Investigation in ARPKD (USG): hyperechoic medulla and loss of corticomedullary differentiation, consistent with small medullary cysts. (Book p789)

items.q: An antenatal ultrasound at 30 weeks shows bilaterally enlarged echogenic kidneys with small medullary cysts and no corticomedullary differentiation, plus oligohydramnios. Which diagnosis fits?
items.exp: ARPKD is autosomal recessive and can be diagnosed in utero with small cysts in the medulla; USG shows hyperechoic medulla with loss of corticomedullary differentiation. (Book p789)

items.q: The cut section of the kidney in ARPKD shows small cysts in the medulla rather than the large cysts typical of ADPKD.
opts: False — ARPKD shows large cortical cysts
False — ARPKD shows a single cyst
items.exp: ARPKD can be diagnosed in utero with small cysts in the medulla (figure 'ARPKD: cut section of kidney'), unlike ADPKD's multiple large cysts. (Book p789)

items.q: A neonate with ARPKD is in respiratory distress with a small chest. The underlying mechanism and outcome described are:
opts: Pulmonary hypoplasia from oligohydramnios — 70% die within 1 year
Pneumothorax from mechanical ventilation — usually survives
items.exp: ARPKD with pulmonary hypoplasia: 70% succumb to death within 1 year, the major cause of death at birth. (Book p789)
